systems.name: Relay v1 brain
systems.summary: Wanders, hunts, searches, chases, breaks doors; never leaves the map.

systems.name: Director (alarm panel)
systems.summary: Scoring core in main, not wired; Relay v2 step V0 (10-29 19:03, inert) brought it up to the 10-07 to 10-14 rules (phone walk, unlock, the rattle, the player-sees-it notice, no rehang) and added the floor-1 first-call hold and a full per-floor disarm. Since 10-30 11:35 (V3a) the director and the v2 loop are built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2, off until the bots pass and Red says yes (C02). Since 10-30 15:15 (V3c) a device tripped in a chase or a door break is heard and queued; it goes out at the next Away.

systems.name: Away, arrive, withdraw
systems.summary: It leaves, stays away, and returns at least 42 m from you. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 11:35 (V3a): arrive, step-in, the give-up beat, patrol from T3, withdraw and away; off until the flip (C02). Since 10-30 V3b adds its door licences (OPEN, BREAK only with a perception licence, WALL), Withdraw's one OPEN and the handoff, all behind the define. Since V4b it keeps one clock through its one look, so a look never buys time (G6).
systems.closed_note: Decided: v2 approved, after the Alpha (10-21)

systems.name: Noise meter
systems.summary: Sprints, barges and slams add up and call it; walking is almost free.

systems.name: Quiet-player sweep
systems.summary: After 240 s with no call it patrols the zone ahead of you. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 (V3b, the Q2 sweep); off until the flip (C02). Since 15:15 (V3c) waypoint 1 is picked where the Relay can step in and every leg keeps W ≥ 21 m, so a sweep no longer ends at its step-in.

systems.name: Tiers
systems.summary: Since 10-29 20:11 (Relay v2 step V1, on today's Relay): one tier per 150 new cells stood in (start rooms, stairwells, X and the station not counted), cap 5, never falls; the 120 s stall rise is gone (C04 a + b). Lamp odds are capped on every tier (stutter ≤ 20 %, failing ≤ 12 %). TIER is off the HUD and the CAUGHT screen (C04 c); only the optional RELAY READOUT assist shows it. The rest of v2's per-tier numbers are in main since 10-29 (V0, inert).

systems.name: Test bots
systems.summary: A tool: seeded bots measure the Relay before and after each step; its 15 measurement fixes are in main since 10-08, and its reports carry rule flags (E1, Floor 1 grace, A12, release cause) since 10-22. A follower mode walks the wall-cue arrows and checks they never point into glass or walls (10-22). The 10-22 smoke on v1 passed 8 of 8 (C05). No full matrix after the double-acting doors (Red 10-22: "不跑直接合"); the 10-08 Step 0 matrix stays the v1 reference. On 10-30 (harness r3.1, 14:44) it measured Floor 1's onboarding, B1's first encounter (2 seeds) and the first define-on smoke (1 seed, 8 runs, V3a + V3b only). The smoke grades no gate: RELAX gained 0 and G8 held on that seed; G5 waits for V4b. V4b's own 8-run smoke (seed 2554, 22:21): 6 chases, 2 lost, none by a bot trying to flee; the evader bots met no chase in 4 runs, so G5 is still unread, and their reaction clock has to start at the cue first.

systems.name: Path hearing
systems.summary: Sound follows real paths: a shut door or window adds 9 m; walls block.

systems.name: Sense links
systems.summary: A heard noise gives a rough estimate, never your exact spot. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 17:37 (V4a): the sense link, the estimate's error, repeats, margin decay and one re-target per 1.5 s; off until the flip (C02).

systems.name: Eyes and spotting
systems.summary: A 120° head cone to 12 m; a meter that fills faster up close. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 22:21 (V4b); off until the flip (C02).

systems.name: Lock-on and chase
systems.summary: Warnings first, a 0.7 s hold and chime (1.7 s on an encounter's first lock-on within 6 m, C37); chase capped at 4.4 m/s; the catch stays 0.7 m. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 22:21 (V4b); off until the flip (C02).
systems.closed_note: Decided: keep 0.7 m, a longer hold on a close first sighting (10-30)

systems.name: Sight tests, prompt gate
systems.summary: Prompts hide only for threats the player can perceive. Live since 10-29 21:22 (Relay v2 step V2, define-free): EXAMINE prompts hide only during a chase and 3 s after it, while a door break's blows are heard within 36 m, or while the Relay is on screen and lit.

systems.name: Warning stages
systems.summary: Walking distance to the Relay sets stages 0 to 2; since 10-22 it drives the W1 lamps and holds the moving wallpaper on plain K00.

systems.name: Stage 1: your lamps
systems.summary: Your room's lamps dip together, never near it (on v1 since 10-22); flickering and failing lamps are held steady (or dim) for the warning and dip with it (M1 + M3, 10-22 20:47). Each burst sags the room-tone hum with them (the ballast groan, since 10-22 15:23).

systems.name: Stage 2: muffled steps
systems.summary: Its steps through walls, muffled by doors, at stage 2 or in sight (+10.3 dB over room tone through a shut door); a faint hum when it stands still (C30). In main since 10-22 15:23.

systems.name: Stage 3: lock-on
systems.summary: A door-holder thunk and one chime when it sees you. The lock-on is built behind the define since 10-30 22:21 (V4b); its sounds are still to do (声音设计).

systems.name: Extra cues
systems.summary: Device sounds, a panel tick, the hum returning, an edge marker.
systems.closed_note: Decided: all; marker off by default (10-21)

systems.name: Chase wave
systems.summary: Lamps ripple out from your room when a chase starts.

systems.name: Wallpaper arrows
systems.summary: The print's arrows turn toward the station TV, then the EXIT (C24 = A + A20), and run with a chase; they never lie (C29) and never glow (A24). Motion: A + M4 + V1 (C31, 10-22). The ambient print motion they sit on is in main since 10-22. Live on desktop since 10-22 21:48, when the route driver landed; phones have turn-only arrows in main since 10-30 23:14 (C34), not yet run on a device, and full arrows wait for a device measure; WebGL shows no cue, and turn-only there is a team call. The station phase is live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (wired 17:33, M5); floors below LEVEL 0 wait for M4.
systems.closed_note: Decided: yes (10-07); the exit is set (10-21)

systems.name: Screens join warnings
systems.summary: Parked, not in v1 (C09, Red 10-22): CRTs would show interference at stage 1 and an alarm slate in a chase. Screens never sag or roll with the lamps.

systems.name: Warnings on today's Relay
systems.summary: Both warnings run on today's Relay since 10-22: W1 lamps and W2 steps. The 2D stingers and clicks are gone, tension follows the stage and the drone is gated (C10, C30).

systems.name: Doors: E open, shut
systems.summary: Doors open on E and shut; each is a noise heard to about 20 m. Double-acting since 10-22 15:11: the leaf always swings away from whoever moves it, every unlock is a push, and an opened door is never broken. Since 10-30 20:44 every double-acting door has a vision panel, map doors included, one form per zone (A42): within 1.0 m of a shut leaf you peek through it, and the peek runs live (C36, A43), with PEEK on the phone's USE disc since 20:51. The Relay can't see through it, and the wired glass can't be broken; you can see the Relay through it, so a lit door no longer counts as cover in the Relay's unseen tests (map side, 20:54). No map door is a Run door: the low square window belongs to the Run! rooms, which are not on the map yet (M8, 系统设计 10-30).
systems.closed_note: Decided: swing away from the player (10-22)

systems.name: Ease, barge, slam, ajar
systems.summary: Walk to open softly; sprint to barge or slam; the Relay leaves doors ajar. The Relay's OPEN, which leaves a door ajar at 30°, is built behind the define since 10-30 (V3b); the player's ease, barge and slam are still to build.

systems.name: Broken doors
systems.summary: Broken for the run; E (or USE on phones, since 10-22) is refused, silent (0.55 s guard). The B·4 crosshair and its knock are live with HUD key B since 10-29 (14:49; sounds 15:31). Decided 10-30 (A41): a broken door tears at its top pivot and leans on the bottom one; a half-broken door stays weak, because the Relay resumes from the blows already struck; steel doors take 0.5 s longer; baked debris; a thin light leak shows in the split. Live since 17:40: the look landed at 17:34 (游戏视觉), the map side at 17:40 (关卡设计: kept blows, a steel door takes one blow more). Its sounds landed at 18:00 (声音设计).

systems.name: Glass and climbing
systems.summary: Hold E to break a pane through staged cracks (a loud call, since 10-21); walk into the frame to climb. Cracks are kept between holds and knocks (since 10-22).

systems.name: Quiet sash pry
systems.summary: Hold E on the latch for 4 s: a quiet way through a window.

systems.name: Alarmed windows
systems.summary: Foil-taped windows that always call the Relay.

systems.name: Door, lock, key models
systems.summary: Since 10-29 20:23 (D1.6 and map contract v9) every map door except the EXIT wears the D1.6 door, lock and key models, every key is the dressed key (the floor key hangs on the station's hook), and the unlock shot uses it; since 10-30 the leaves are walnut.

systems.name: Locked doors
systems.summary: Locks, rattle, key-turn shot; in play it now locks only Floor 1's EXIT, until the floor key (A13, since 10-29 19:17); inner doors stay unlocked (A13, A35).

systems.name: Keys
systems.summary: Look and E on desktop, USE or a tap on phones (both since 10-22 16:45). Today one per zone, opening nothing; decided 10-22: one floor key per floor, at the station. The floor key is live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (in main since 16:58): one 'Key · floor' at the station's key spot, opening the EXIT and any locked door on its floor. In a station run, floors below LEVEL 0 build no zone keys and lock no inner doors (A35, since 17:49).

systems.name: Map, zones, modules
systems.summary: Generated zones, rooms as data, streaming, the Level Designer. Level transitions (frames and renovated crossings) are in main since 10-30 21:37, inert until 关卡设计's map contract lands (A47).

systems.name: Trigger rooms
systems.summary: Rooms you can read from the doorway; entering sounds an alarm.

systems.name: Sanctuaries
systems.summary: Dead-circuit rooms the Relay will not enter.

systems.name: Relay entries
systems.summary: Where it arrives and leaves; markers live, dead-end entries to build.

systems.name: Map validator
systems.summary: Checks keys can be reached, windows stay passable, cover exists.

systems.name: Office dressing
systems.summary: Cubicles, CRTs, piles and wall outlets (in the maze since 10-22); terminal host desks to come.

systems.name: Run! rooms
systems.summary: The alarm corridor: a long trigger room entered through an arch, ending in a door you can shut. Stepping in calls the Relay, and the sprint to the door is the reward. Its look B Emergency Power was decided 10-21 and its kit was built in a clone. Still to come: the trigger room framework, the module, and Red's calls 2 to 8. Run doors and the low square window arrive with it (M8). Dates (schedule R2, re-dated 10-31): an inert kit in main by 11-03; a first playable room only after 关卡设计's map hooks (CR-1 to CR-6, M8), at the earliest 11-04 if they land by 11-02; off in the PT4 playtest snapshot. The trip sounds only the devices' own local sounds, no building bell (C07). The goal door is RN-F with set A's F5 window, never locked; RN-X is retired. Run! is the tier-2 trigger kind, after the run's first send, and keeps the trigger rooms' shared tell at its entrance (系统设计, 10-31). Red decided calls 2 and 5–8 on 10-31 (C38–C43): its own goal door, Office hosts allowed, the title-stream room left alone, no EXIT sign inside, a glowing goal window, and three reference photos.
systems.closed_note: Decided: look B Emergency Power (10-21); gets a date (10-30)

systems.name: Bathroom rooms
systems.summary: Bathroom rooms around a pool (A48). Nothing is built, and the game has no water yet. Research landed 10-31 00:26 (research/bathroom_rooms/). Its 20_for_red.md asks Red D1–D12, and D1–D4 and D8 block the build. Build (schedule R4a/R4b): a playable greybox by 11-05, the v1 look and sound by 11-09, about 129–183 planned hours.

systems.name: Evacuation plan
systems.summary: One printed sheet in the first room by the desk on Floor 1 (A26), with a copy on every stairwell landing; EXAMINE reads it. Red picked sheet A on 10-22: a route diagram that teaches four rules and the locked stair (a Phase 0 variant where the stair is not locked). Since 10-29 19:17 Floor 1's sheet hangs in the first room (the room sheet while the EXIT is locked); floors without a station keep the Phase 0 sheet at the start door (since 10-22 21:03).

systems.name: EXAMINE close-up
systems.summary: E frames the plan or the first key; the game pauses (in main since 10-22); phones open it with USE (READ) and leave with BACK (since 10-22 21:10), a TEXT chip shows the transcript, and zoom works (wheel or right button; pinch or double tap on phones; since 10-24); its sound mix is in since 10-22 12:23 (声音设计's sound_inspect_v2); a focus-loss guard remains. Since 10-30 15:22 only careful reading pauses (A43): the plan, memos and terminal pages pause. Close-ups for looking run live (the first key, one-line signs and the station TV's ad), and a threat or a catch ends them; the door peek has no threat gate (C36). On phones a live close-up has no TEXT chip, no pause button and no back latch, so backing away is one move (since 15:31). A live close-up keeps the live mix (since 18:00). Since 10-30 21:39 a close-up faces its object square on from every side, the station TV keeps its old angle, and one more tap shows the content alone, full bleed (A46).

systems.name: Office terminals
systems.summary: One readable computer per Office zone; E to read its pages. Decided 10-30: the era's own interaction, a DOS text-mode in-house program with CUA keys and a lightbar menu (C19; spec research/computer_ui/41_c19_period_interaction.md); our own 8 × 16 bitmap face (C20; FR816 C20, in main since 14:48); on phones the close-up is full bleed with no TEXT chip or transcript (A39); readable terminals show E·1 (A38). Built in main since 10-30 13:49 (游戏视觉's terminal_a: the 80 × 25 char-grid terminal, MAIN / DOC / LIST / HELP, the READ close-up at 70 % with TEXT on desktop and iPad, 95 % without on phones), inert until a desk calls it (关卡设计's L2; the close-up's input branch landed 10-30 15:22, touch tap and swipe 15:42). The strings are in since 14:57, three more memo sets since 15:24, and the program is named OFFICE MEMO (INTEROFFICE was a real Oracle product).

systems.name: Crosshair states
systems.summary: One grammar for door, lock, broken door and the look-eye, live with HUD key B since 10-29 14:49 (the map's AimKind feed, Read/Examine E·1). The station-TV eye (C35) is live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (in main since 16:41; E · WATCH TV on the playing station TV since 10-30 15:23, WATCH on the phone's USE disc since 15:31, A44). Readable computer terminals show E·1 too, and dark or still desk screens never (A38, 10-30; to build with the terminals).

systems.name: Key and lock HUD motion
systems.summary: HUD key B is live since 10-29 14:49: the key slides in (on the instant pickup the glyph plays P4 alone, KP-1b), and the padlock opens at the crosshair; the unlock shot keeps the panel, C27 (d). Its sounds are live since 15:31 (flight, land, lock tug, unlock drop, broken door).

systems.name: Desk monitors
systems.summary: Ad_03 (WTCZ, since 10-22) plays on the desk monitors of floors without a station; decided 10-22: still screens in the maze, the ad only on the title and station TVs. On Floor 1, since 10-29 19:17, the desk monitors show still screens and the station TV plays the ad with its READ close-up (R3).

systems.name: Exit and win
systems.summary: One EXIT per floor; a stairwell behind it leads one floor deeper (LEVEL 0, then B1, B2, ...); a run ends only when caught; the tier carries over (in main since 10-22 15:39). The stairwell safe zone is in main since 16:05 (A27): no sight, catch or hearing inside, a chase ends at its door, and the Relay stops there, then walks off; since 17:06 its sound agrees (no hum or groan inside, tension at its floor). The lock and the floor key (A13) are live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (in main since 16:58): the EXIT is locked from the floor's start and opens with the floor key and the unlock shot. In a station run, floors below LEVEL 0 keep an unlocked EXIT until they get their own stations (A35).
systems.closed_note: Decided: an EXIT per floor leads deeper (10-21)

systems.name: Exit signs
systems.summary: Lit, dim and loose EXIT signs; the LIT-locked one over each floor's EXIT is in main since 10-22 15:39 (C23 step 1); chevron signs in its zone later.
systems.closed_note: Decided: a lit sign over the exit door, chevrons in its zone later (10-22)

systems.name: Way-out route
systems.summary: The route the arrows point: the station until the floor key is taken, then the EXIT; one field shared with the TV beacon, glass impassable, never reads the Relay. In main since 10-22 21:48 (Wayfinding, spec v1.0.3). The station phase is live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (wired 17:33, M5): the route and the beacon lead to the station TV until the take, then to the EXIT. A floor without a station (below LEVEL 0 until M4) routes to the EXIT. Since 10-29 19:33 every Tall hall has one doorless arch to a lower neighbour (C33 = 2), so the arrows can lead into it; its other borders stay windows, and R7 fell from 41.9 % to 5.0 % of Tall cells with no arrow (Standard 0.5 %, Low 0.2 %; 关卡设计调研, 10-29).
systems.closed_note: Decided: the station first, then the EXIT (10-22); a door into every Tall hall (10-29)

systems.name: Plan legend
systems.summary: The plan's legend; sheet A (picked 10-22) marks the stair as EXIT. A wall legend that returns with W6 must never show a glowing wall (A24).

systems.name: Plan and alarm pages
systems.summary: A floor plan and alarm history on terminals, later.

systems.name: Touch controls
systems.summary: USE button (it shows broken doors), tap to open, three gaits on every platform since 10-30 (A36): on desktop hold Shift for the slow gait and Ctrl to run, the run goes ahead only (±70°), a normal walk is heard (9 m a step) and the slow gait is silent; pads and keyboards work on phones and iPads, and the stick hides when one is used (10-29); keys by USE or tap since 10-22; the caught card counts KEYS TAKEN. Phone control hints since 10-22 20:2x (X2): the stick teaches SLOW · UNHEARD until it is learned, and the legend shows on the title and, since 10-24, as CONTROLS › GESTURES in the pause sheet, which is now the settings menu. Since 10-24 the layout fits the iPhone Duo's outer and inner screens and keeps the HUD 16 pt clear of rounded corners.

systems.name: Reduce flashing, captions
systems.summary: Lamp changes ramp slower; sounds get captions.

systems.name: More settings
systems.summary: Lamps still, warning-cue volume, visual sound cues, screen effects. Since 10-24 the menu has four tabs (GRAPHICS · COMFORT · CONTROLS · ASSIST) and render-quality presets on every platform (A28); Esc on desktop and the pause on phones open it directly, because the PAUSED card is gone (Red, 10-24), and END RUN returns to the title without asking (A37, 10-30); CONTROLS holds a remappable desktop key map (10-29); the four items above are still to design. The language page comes with P6.

systems.name: Photosafety limits
systems.summary: No lamp may flash more than 3 times a second. Every flicker mode stays at or under 2 a second, and a per-lamp limiter holds 3 as a hard cap (in main since 10-22, 关卡设计 M2; measured: no lamp over 3). W1's dips pass too.

systems.name: WebGL tier
systems.summary: A separate, lighter web build; never changes desktop.

systems.name: Languages
systems.summary: The game's reading layer in nine languages, chosen on one row in the settings: only the chosen language is open, the rest are icons (A45). FrontRooms has no localization today: every string is hard-coded English. Decided 10-30: the world stays English, the menus, HUD, captions and TEXT panel translate, through a small in-house table. In main since 10-30 20:55 (the table, the fonts, translated captions, the language row, AI drafts for eight languages), hidden while English is the only finished language. The strings are still being wrapped by their owners.
systems.closed_note: Decided: nine languages, the world stays English (10-30)

systems.name: Station and TV beacon
systems.summary: One station per floor (on Floor 1 it is the first room, A26): the only TV playing, heard through the building. Its rack holds the floor key; taking it kills the TV, turns the route to the EXIT and calls the hunter to the station, unless the run's first send has not happened yet (A40). Live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (the joint switch-on): the station code (15:08), the floor key and its take (M3, M6, 16:58), the playing TV and its READ close-up (R3, 16:41), the beacon's sound near and far (17:24), and the route and beacon target (M5, 17:33). 游戏视觉's station look (19:11) dresses the room and makes the TV the beacon. Floors below LEVEL 0 get theirs in the next batch (A49, BS1 to BS13) and play as A35 until one lands.

systems.name: Tutorial floor
systems.summary: Floor 1 teaches the loop. Live since 10-29 19:17 (the joint switch-on; in main since 15:08): the station is the first room, the EXIT 7–8 cells away, the station is not a zone, and since 10-30 12:41 (A40) no Relay comes on Floor 1 until you have explored 150 cells (not counting the station) or played 3 min after the start door's shut. The key take no longer triggers that first send. The run's first send keeps C32's gentle arrival, anchored on you and the FLOW target, and comes on B1 if you leave Floor 1 first. Since 16:58 the EXIT is locked from the floor's start and the floor key opens it with the unlock shot (M3), and taking the key kills the TV and turns the arrows to the EXIT; a Relay already out is called to the station (A14). The third-zone fallback is dropped (A40). Bots on 10-30 (v1): an arrow-follower is at the EXIT 16.6 s after Space, so its first encounter is on B1; wanderers reach 150 cells in 125–154 s. Every first chase in those runs was a catch (8 of 8), but only the two evader06 runs try to flee, and both started inside 6 m. Today's sight usually first sees the player at a corner about 6 m away. On B1 (14:44, 2 seeds) evader06 escaped 1 of 2: the escape started at 12 m. Since 15:15 (V3c) the first send's lamps come on as it arrives (C32). C37 (10-30) keeps the 0.7 m catch and adds a longer hold on a close first sighting, behind the define.
systems.closed_note: Decided: E1; first send at 22–30 m (10-22)

decisions.question: Do screens join the warning language?
decisions.recommendation: No in v1
decisions.rationale: Asked by 平面视觉 · 广告 as its SCREENS §4 question. Why not in v1: each cue keeps one meaning, the lamps and steps are not even in yet, and a third channel would muddy what the next playtest can tell apart. The tutorial TV beacon (N6, 10-22) is a broadcast, not a warning: it ducks under every warning, so "one meaning per cue" still holds.

The 2D stingers go in the same sound pass as W2.

decisions.question: Floor 1: the first lamp burst comes after a prompt player is through the EXIT. Send the first Relay closer?
decisions.recommendation: Yes: Floor 1 first send only, 1 s after the take, unseen, just inside stage 1 (22 to 30 m)
decisions.rationale: Today's rule (A14, ≥ 42 m, 3 s after the take) gives a player who walks straight back no W1 on Floor 1: the Relay hunts at 2.6 m/s and the player walks at 3.2, so W only closes while they stand still. From 42 m it needs about 4.6 s to reach the 30 m entry, so the first burst comes 7.9 s or more after the take, while the walk back (2–6 cells) plus the unlock (1.55 s) is done by about 3.5–7.5 s. Sent at 22–30 m after 1 s, stage 1 starts on arrival and the first burst falls 1.3–2 s after the take. That is honest, because it really is near; the Floor 1 grace still bars a chase before a burst. It breaks v2's 42 m Arrive rule for this one send only. Alternatives: a station farther past the EXIT does not help (the gap never closes while the player walks); keeping 42 m and extending the grace to Floor 2 teaches W1 by the placard only; a scripted burst on the take would make the lamps lie.
decisions.answer: 1: Floor 1's first send only, 1 s after the take, unseen, at 22–30 m, on the station's far side from the EXIT and never within 2 cells of the walk back (fallback 18–34 m, then ≥ 14 cells, logged); the station keeps ≥ 2 Steady lamps by its entrance (retimed by A26 on 10-22: on Floor 1 the first send now comes when you leave the first room, 2 cells out of the room with the key taken (the start door's shut does not count), from the far side, with the 150 s fallback; the rest holds) (amended 10-30 by A40: the gentle arrival now belongs to the run's first send wherever it happens, on Floor 1 after the onboarding threshold or on B1 if the player leaves first; it no longer follows the key take, and its step-in uses the tier's arrive delay, 3 s at T1, ruled by 系统设计 for 关卡设计; its placement is anchored on the player and the FLOW target; landed 10-30 12:41) (10-30 15:15, V3c, live on every path: rungs 1 and 2 also need W ≤ 30 m at the cell, so the lamps warn as it arrives; on seed 20388 the first warning went from 51.3 s after the send to 0.02 s)

decisions.ref: RELAY §9.6 (Tall-hall threshold); MAP_ROUTE_SPEC R7; Wayfinding audit s17_way
decisions.question: Tall halls connect only through windows, so the arrows go still in 42 % of their cells. Accept it, or add a door to every Tall hall?
decisions.recommendation: 1, accept: Tall halls stay window-gated and uncued; lamps, groan and steps still warn
decisions.rationale: The arrows never point at glass, because breaking glass calls the Relay. Tall zones border the rest of the floor only through windows (RELAY map facts), which is what makes the window choice (pry quietly for 4 s, or break and call it) matter. 关卡设计's Wayfinding build, measured by 关卡设计调研 over 100 seeds x 3 floors: Tall zones 41.9 % of built cells with no arrow (58.1 % frontier-routed, 0 % target-routed); Low 0.6 %, Standard 1.5 %. §9.6 set about 25 % (of warning time, not cells) as the point to revisit, through a map rule, not the cue. Options: 1 accept (no cost; Tall halls read as the place where the building's guidance runs out; watch the playtest item 'I knew where to go next'); 2 a generator rule giving every Tall zone at least one door or arch to a non-Tall neighbour (关卡设计: generator, validator and re-verification; the window gate and the glass features matter less). Wayfinding lands either way. If Red wants the time-based number first (stage-1 seconds with no arrow in Tall halls), 关卡设计调研's follower bot can measure it once Wayfinding is in main. Asked by 系统设计 in its own chat on 2026-10-22.
decisions.answer: 2: every Tall zone gets at least one door or arch to a non-Tall neighbour, so the wall arrows reach Tall halls. A generator and validator rule (关卡设计), then one test round (rule 22) and 关卡设计调研's R7 re-measure. The windows stay a second way in (pry or break), so the window choice weighs less. Built on 10-29 19:33: each Tall zone has one doorless arch to a lower neighbour (692 of 692 Tall zones over 100 seeds); R7 then fell from 41.9 % to 5.0 % (关卡设计调研). (Red in the 系统设计 chat, 10-29 18:03: "选 2，改地图生成规则：每个高层区至少要有一扇门或一个拱口通向别的区域…", then "不选1", after first clicking 1)

So V4b adds about 1 s and 1.3 m takes away about 0.15 s. Options: 1 keep 0.7 m and finish V4b; 2 go to 1.3 m now (游戏视觉's HR16: it reads as a reach, but Hunter B is not in main, so that gain cannot be seen yet); 3 option 1 plus about 1 s more on a first sighting inside 6 m (a small V4b change; it gives more time closer in, 3.2 s at 5.9 m against 2.2 s at 6.1 m). Asked by 系统设计 in its own chat on 2026-10-30.

glossary.definition: The director’s noise meter for one run. Player noises add to it: sprint step +3, barge +8, slam +12, pry +8, ease a door or unlock +1, walking 0. It drains 3 per second (2 at tier 5), starting 3 s after the last noise. At the threshold (60 at tier 1, down to 45 at tier 5) the Relay is called to the area of the noise, never to the exact spot.

How much threat the player has perceived in the current encounter. Only perceived cues count: lamps +1/s, steps +2.5/s, seeing the Relay +4/s, the chase +6/s, a lock-on +15. At the peak the director holds for 4 s (SUSTAIN), then fades the encounter and the Relay withdraws.
A difficulty step. Today it rises with zones visited plus a stall rule; v2 proposes one tier per 150 newly explored cells. Tiers make the Relay better, never the warnings shorter.

The Relay may lock on only after the warning has run continuously for at least 3 s (stage 1 or higher), including at least 1 s of continuous stage 2 (steps). The timers reset when the stage drops. Only a lock-on at touching distance (1.5 m) is exempt.

The Relay’s distance to the player along real walking paths (a shut door adds 9 m), never more than three times the straight line. It sets the warning stages: stage 1 at 30 m or less, stage 2 at 18 m or less.
The guaranteed calm after the Relay leaves: 100 s at tier 1, 60 s at tier 5. Noise cannot call it back during RELAX; glass and alarm devices still can.

The Relay may break a door only if a sound it heard came through that door, or it saw the player cross it or heard it move. It may quietly open the doors that were shut on its route when it was sent. Any other shut door is a wall to it.
When a quiet player goes 240 s (tier 1) without a call, the director sends the Relay to patrol a zone ahead of them, aimed at the area, never the exact spot.
The warning level in the player’s own room: 0 nothing, 1 lamps dip, 2 muffled steps, 3 the lock-on chime.
The director sending the Relay toward an area, because Attention crossed its threshold, a device was tripped, or a sweep is due.
